analysis.title: Strat Chat: Bond markets rally, but inflation risks persist
key_insights: Government bonds rallied in October on French fiscal concerns and weaker risk sentiment, but resilient data and inflation risks have since driven a renewed sell-off led by the US.
Global sovereign yields have risen above levels implied by a simple macro fundamentals model (chart of the month).
The fund added UK duration via 10-year gilt futures because gilts look relatively cheap versus other government bond markets after the sell-off.
Australian rates are a high-conviction position. Duration long was taken back to about 1.5 years versus benchmark, with further RBA hikes seen as unlikely and cuts possible from H2 2027.
In Europe the fund still favours German bonds over France and Italy, with a smaller relative position. The France-Germany yield gap has widened on French fiscal uncertainty.
The fund added Paraguayan local bonds after a sell-off triggered by the collapse of a major domestic bank, seeing no evidence of contagion.
US inflation exposure was increased because market expectations fell despite resilient growth. Medium-term pricing may underestimate upside risks, including renewed energy-driven inflation.
The fund stays selective in UK and European inflation, where pricing already reflects a higher inflation path.
Currency stance is defensive with a long USD bias and fewer EM currency longs. Higher developed-market yields could weigh on EM FX.
New short South African rand on weaker terms of trade. The yen short against the euro was closed and profits were taken on the AUD short.
The fund remains underweight developed-market credit as valuations offer limited protection. Heavy tech issuance pressures longer maturities.
October gross return was 2.41% versus 1.70% for the benchmark, driven by credit, currencies and inflation. Duration detracted.
